rationale: B wins because it has the discipline to kill angles that sound clever but do not yet have the reporting spine to stand up. A's "Why a private Mindbody bundled its AI feature instead of charging extra for it" is smart bait, but its own proof list admits it does not know who owns Mindbody, when the deal closed, or whether this pricing choice is unusual. B's refusal of "Take-private / exit-path angle" and "Bundled pricing / AI monetization angle" is the boring adult move here. It still needs edits, especially "rolling out to 50,000 studios," but it gives the founder fewer shiny ways to embarrass himself.
gaps_in_A: "treats 50,000 studios' booking calendars as one data set" overclaims the data architecture. The update says Mindbody has 50,000 studios and uses booking data; it does not say calendars are pooled into one cross-studio data set.
"private-equity ownership" is not grounded. The update says Mindbody is privately held after a take-private deal, not who owns it or whether a PE monetization thesis is driving AI pricing.

"The AI upgrade boutique fitness startups promised" depends on unnamed AI-native challengers and promises not in the update. If the proof item says you still need a competitor, the headline is running ahead of the facts.
"adding AI to both" overstates the ClassPass connection. The facts support a studio-side tool and ClassPass ownership; they do not support AI being added to ClassPass or shared data flows.
gaps_in_B: "rolling out to 50,000 Studios" overstates reach. Mindbody powers over 50,000 studios and salons; the update does not say every one gets, enables, or uses this assistant.

"While Fitness Apps Race to Build AI Coaches" imports a market narrative not supplied in the update. It can work only after the founder supplies real contrast cases, not because the phrase sounds trend-piece ready.
"now the AI That Fills Both" overclaims the ClassPass tie. The set later asks whether the systems are separate, which means the headline should not imply the answer.

The next step is muddy: it says `journalist-fit-check`, then admits the 22% pilot claim and ClassPass relationship must be verified first. Verification is the next step; target matching comes after the floor stops wobbling.
